flags.title: 229 Federally Recognized Alaska Native Tribes — ANCSA Land Structure
flags.summary: Alaska has 229 federally recognized tribes — the most of any state by a factor of 6. ANCSA (1971) transferred land to regional and village corporations (for-profit entities), not tribal governments. Most villages have no reservation land. Route: ANTHC (907-729-1900), IHS Alaska (907-729-3686), Regional Corps: CIRI (907-274-8638), Doyon (907-452-4755), NANA (907-442-3301), Sealaska (907-586-1512).

flags.title: Bush Alaska — 75% of Communities NOT Connected to Road System
flags.summary: 75% of Alaska communities are off-road. Villages in Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta, Arctic Slope, Interior, Southeast accessible only by small aircraft. Intake: confirm communication method (satellite phone, village phone, community broadband), identify nearest hub city (Bethel, Fairbanks, Nome, Kodiak, Juneau), route to ALSC first (907-272-9431). Do NOT assume in-person routing is viable.

flags.title: Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend (PFD) — Annual Income Supplement Creates Eligibility Gaps
flags.summary: Annual PFD payment (~$1,000-$2,000/year; 2023: ~$1,312) counted as income for benefit eligibility in the year received. October payment may create temporary Medicaid/SNAP gaps. Help clients maximize this annual payment. Apply: pfd.alaska.gov (907-465-2326).

flags.title: Alaska UI — $370/Week Maximum, Lowest Expansion State in Registry
flags.summary: Alaska UI max $370/week — lowest of any expansion state (lower than many non-expansion states). Duration: 26 weeks. Appeal deadline: 30 days (longest in registry), but contact ALSC within 15 days of any denial regardless.

flags.title: Rural Alaska — Violence Against Women, Alaska Native Women at Highest Risk
flags.summary: Alaska has among the highest DV/sexual assault rates in the US. Alaska Native women disproportionately victimized. Rural proximity to perpetrators + lack of law enforcement = extreme danger. Resources: ANWRC (907-745-4728), STAR Anchorage (907-276-7279), VPSO local contacts. Emergency transportation funding available through some DV organizations.

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: Alaska 72-Hour Hold
flags.message: AK involuntary psychiatric hold law: Alaska 72-Hour Hold. Statutory authority: AS 47.30.705. Maximum initial hold duration: 72 hours. Legal standard: likelihood of serious harm. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 72 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in AK retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in AK: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: Alaska Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: Alaska Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
